chunks: When the mu'adhdhin says, 'The salat has been established,' do the people stand on their feet, or do they remain seated until their Imam comes?
He عليه السلام said: No; rather, they should stand on their feet. If their Imam comes, then so be it; otherwise, a man from among the people should be taken by the hand and brought forward.

key_terms.إِمَامُهُمْ: their prayer leader in the congregational salat
key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنُ: the caller who announces the prayer and iqamah
key_terms.فَلْيُؤْخَذْ بِيَدِ رَجُلٍ: a man should be selected and brought forward
key_terms.فَيُقَدَّمَ: he is put forward to lead the congregation
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: the iqamah phrase indicating that the salat has been established
key_terms.يَقُومُونَ: they stand up in preparation for prayer

ai.seo_question: When the mu'adhdhin says 'qad qāmati al-ṣalāh,' should the congregation stand or wait seated for the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling concerning the conduct of the congregation when the iqamah reaches the phrase indicating that the salat has been established. The congregation should stand rather than remain seated, and if the designated Imam does not arrive, one man from among them should be advanced to lead the congregational prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "When the muezzin (caller to prayer) says 'The prayer has been established' (during the iqamah), should the people stand up or remain seated until their Imam arrives?"
He (as) replied: "No, they should stand up. If their Imam arrives, they proceed with him; otherwise, a man from among the congregation should be taken by the hand and brought forward to lead."
